title: Rules Before Oracles: Auditable, User-Configurable Argument Selection for Deliberative Polling
abstract: arXiv:2608.23979v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In a deliberative poll, once submissions outnumber what anyone will read, some mechanism chooses which arguments each voter sees, acquiring much of the decision; practice delegates it to opaque learned rankers, so a voter cannot recompute or contest the exposure that shaped their vote. We ask whether it can be a published rule over publicly recomputable evidence with parameters held by the voter, treating legibility as an admissibility condition on usable mechanisms, not an objective traded against accuracy. We formalise a poll over bipolar justification sets, judging a slate by reason coverage, the order it arrives in, and captured endorsement mass; we give seven checkable criteria for a civic recommender and a rule meeting them: a one-hop reversed endorsement flow parameterised by a relation-weight function. An agentic simulator records every slate at every vote, over about 17,000 seed-paired runs. Served slates fall 0.035 short of a l

translated_title: 规则优先于神谕：用于协商式民调的可审计、用户可配置的论据选择
translated_abstract: 在协商式民调中，一旦提交的论据数量超过任何人能够阅读的范围，就需要某种机制来决定每位选民看到哪些论据，这实际上承担了大部分决策权；实践中，这一机制往往被委托给不透明的学习排序器，导致选民无法重新计算或质疑影响其投票的曝光内容。我们提出，这一机制是否可以是一条公开规则，基于可公开重新计算的证据，且参数由选民持有——将可读性视为可用机制的准入条件，而非与准确性进行权衡的目标。我们形式化了一种围绕双极论证集进行的民调，通过理由覆盖度、到达顺序以及所捕获的支持度质量来评判一组候选论据；我们为公民推荐器提出了七项可检验的标准，并给出一个满足这些标准的规则：一种由关系权重函数参数化的单跳反向支持流。一个代理模拟器记录了每次投票中的每一组论据，涵盖约17,000次种子配对运行。所呈现的论据组与最优结果相差0.035。
tldr: 本文提出一种可审计、用户可配置的论据选择规则，以公开可验证的方式替代不透明排序器，确保协商民调的曝光过程可被选民重新计算和质疑。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an auditable, user-configurable argument selection rule that replaces opaque rankers with publicly verifiable evidence, ensuring the exposure process in deliberative polls can be recomputed and contested by voters.
